Congrats on getting this moving — quick note from the onboarding/eval side so expectations are clear. I’ve sketched an evaluation plan and owner list below; I’ll add this to the MAP draft and share an updated PDF after the kickoff.

Proposed evaluation plan (owners):
- Sample traffic ingestion + validation (Dev Singh, Nebula) — deliver: 24h trace + schema
- Baseline test (Redwood test harness) — owner: Marissa Cole — deliver: P95/P99 latency, tokens/hour, failure rates
- Throughput stress run (pilot pool) — owner: Vivek Kulkarni — deliver: steady-state throughput numbers and GPU utilization
- Quality regression checks (sample prompts) — owner: Laura Bennett — deliver: pass/fail on 20 golden prompts
- Security/compliance evidence (logs, retention) — owner: Sean Gallagher / Legal liaison — deliver: checklist + retention plan

Success criteria (examples — we can refine together):
- P95 latency for production prompt set ≤ 200 ms
- P99 latency ≤ 500 ms for 1KB average prompt length
- Sustained throughput target: ≥ 1.5M tokens/hour for the baseline model under the pilot configuration
- No data egress or retention issues in sample audit

I’ve updated throughput_model.xlsx with a suggested starting pool of H100 instances and a conservative warm-up plan — Vivek, please correct sizing if you want different assumptions before the kickoff.

I’ll bring a short runbook to the kickoff showing what we need from Nebula to get the baseline test done in 72 hours after the meeting.

— Marissa

Subject: Re: Kicking off MAP — technical sizing notes

Adding a few technical notes ahead of kickoff so we can use a focused agenda:

1) Sizing assumptions:
- If Nebula’s sample trace averages ~1KB prompts and the baseline model is a 13B transformer, our conservative starting point is a 4–6 GPU pool (H100) for the pilot to reach the 1.5M tokens/hour target with headroom for caching. Exact numbers depend on tokenization and KV cache hit rates.

2) Quantization + perf:
- 4-bit int8/4 implementations can reduce memory pressure and increase effective throughput but introduce small quality delta. We should run a quick quality check on 20 golden prompts if we quantize.

3) Test harness & metrics we’ll collect:
- P95/P99 latency, GPU utilization, avg tokens/sec, KV cache hit rate, error codes by route

4) Need from Nebula before pilot:
- 48–72h sample traffic (anonymized), a list of top-10 prompt templates, and expected concurrency profiles (RPS).

I’ll bring an initial pilot config and a stress-run script to the kickoff. Linking the shared drive folder here: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/nebula-MAP-RED-NEB-2026-009

If the 12/22 10:00 PT kickoff is set, I can block a 1-hour deep-dive immediately after the meeting to walk through the throughput_model assumptions.

— Vivek
